items.name: Benchlight Solution
items.description: A working light the colour of old chalk. It picks out cut channels and worn inlay far better than it lights a road.

effects.description: A flat grey-white light that shows detail rather than distance.

items.name: Annotated Light
items.description: A close, warm reading light that makes ink stand off a page. Useless outdoors and indispensable at a desk.

effects.description: A tight working light that shows writing rather than distance.

items.name: Marginalia Lantern
items.description: Under it, the notes somebody pencilled in a margin twenty years ago and then erased come back faintly. Ione has asked that this not be sold outside the tower.

effects.description: Raises writing that is no longer strictly on the page.

items.name: Coldread Solution
items.description: A flat white light with no warmth in it. It flatters nothing and hides nothing, which is the entire requirement when the page you are reading has been lied about.

effects.description: Cold even light that shows a surface exactly as it is.

items.name: Second Reading
items.description: A dull, patient little light that shows the inside of a bottle rather than the room. Ione has started asking for the failures instead of the successes and will not explain.

effects.description: A close working light for looking at what went wrong.

items.name: Ghostline Solution
items.description: A thin blue-grey light that ignores ink entirely and shows only pressure — where a nib pushed, where a page was leaned on, where something was written and then taken away. It cannot read. It can only point at the fact that there was something to read.

effects.description: A raking light that finds the impression rather than the mark.

items.name: Handmark Solution
items.description: Held over a page it sorts the hands: everything one person wrote goes cold and everything the next wrote stays warm. The archive holds a great many pages with two hands on them and has never had a way of saying so.

effects.description: A close reading light that separates one hand from another.

items.name: Tablewide Reading
items.description: Splashed, the hand-sorting light stops being a lamp you hold over one page and becomes a thing you lay a whole table under. Ione put eleven months of loose sheets out at once and did not speak for some time.

effects.description: Sorts hands across everything laid out rather than one page at a time.

items.name: Double-Read Solution
items.description: Two finished lights folded into one another rather than brewed from leaf. It shows a page under cold even light and under raking light at the same time, which no single pour has ever managed and which Ione says is the difference between reading a page and reading what happened to it.

effects.description: Cold and raking light at once — surface and pressure together.
